_comment: How this language's PRONUNCIATION becomes its transliteration. Read by lib/translit.py; optional, like every file of this name.
_prefer: WHICH PRONUNCIATION. Wiktionary carries several per word, tagged by register: Classical-Persian, Dari, Kabuli, Tajik and Iran. The classical one is where kitāb, xwāndan and dōst come from -- it is a correct romanisation of a Persian nobody in Tehran speaks, and it is also what the source's own `translit` field holds, which is why every gloss came out in it. docs/lang/fa.md romanises what is actually said, so the Iran reading is the one this edition wants.
_map: Longest match first, so t͡ʃ is č before t is t and ɒː is ā before ɒ. The vowel inventory of docs/lang/fa.md is a e o ā i u and nothing else, so every IPA vowel lands on one of those.
_drop: Stress, syllable dots, the brackets a transcription is written in, and the secondary articulations Wiktionary's narrow transcriptions carry -- aspiration, palatalisation, labialisation. [kʰʲe.t̪ʰɒ́ːb̥] is ketāb once those are gone.
_ow: و is v as a consonant (varzeš) and w inside the diphthong ow (nowruz). Longest match settles it: `ow` is matched before `w`.
_strip_leading: Every Persian word that begins with a vowel begins with a glottal stop -- آب is [ʔɒːb] -- and nobody writes it: آب is āb. In the MIDDLE of a word it is written, because there it distinguishes (بعد ba'd), so only a leading one goes.
_roman: Wiktionary romanises a Persian INFLECTED FORM in its form table -- میسازم is mí-sâzam -- and that is the one thing the pronunciation cannot give, because it is recorded per lemma. It writes long a as â and marks stress with an acute; this edition writes ā and marks no stress. The acute is dropped and â becomes ā, in that order, so that the macron of ā is not dropped with it. It writes غ as ġ where docs/lang/fa.md writes q for both ق and غ (24 verb tables and many form rows), so ġ becomes q. WHICH OF A FORM'S ROWS: `prefer` is the pattern of an Iranian romanisation -- a mí-/mi- present, or one with â and none of ā ī ū ē ō ḗ -- and the first row that matches is taken (lib/translit.py form_sound): some verbs have the Dari table first, so نمی‌دانستم came out dānistam, شنیدم šunīdam, ایستادم īstādam. `after_last` is where a cell's second reading starts: the source writes بود as `būd /bud`, the classical first, and the part after the last / is taken.
